summary: This mishnah lists the mitzvos of Sukkos and for how many days each one is done: lulav and aravah, Hallel and simcha, sukkah and pouring water on the mizbe'ach, and the flute.

chunks.en: The lulav and the aravah:
chunks.st: The lulav is taken and the altar is encircled together with the willow branch

chunks.en: six or seven days.
chunks.explain: It depends on which day is Shabbos.
chunks.st: either six or seven days,
chunks.stMore: depending on which day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat.

chunks.en: Hallel and the simcha:
chunks.explain: Simcha here means eating from the korban shelamim.
chunks.st: The obligation to recite the full hallel and the mitzva of rejoicing,
chunks.stMore: i.e., eating the meat of the peace-offering,

chunks.en: eight days. The sukkah and pouring the water on the mizbe'ach:
chunks.st: is in effect for eight days, seven days of Sukkot and the Eighth Day of Assembly. The mitzva of sukka and the ritual of the water libation

chunks.en: seven days. And the flute:
chunks.st: on the altar are in effect for seven days. The flute

chunks.en: five or six days.
chunks.st: is played in the Temple for five or six days,
chunks.stMore: depending on which day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat, to enhance the rejoicing on the Festival.

summary: We take the lulav for seven days only when the first day of Sukkos is on Shabbos. Otherwise it is six days, because we do not take it on a Shabbos in the middle of Sukkos.

chunks.en: How is the lulav seven days?
chunks.st: The lulav is taken for seven days. How so?

chunks.en: If the first day of
chunks.st: If the first day of

chunks.en: the chag falls on Shabbos,
chunks.explain: On the first day the lulav is a mitzvah from the Torah, so we take it even on Shabbos.
chunks.st: the Festival occurs on Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: since the mitzva to take the lulav on the first day is a mitzva by Torah law, it overrides Shabbat and one takes the lulav that day.

chunks.en: the lulav is seven days.
chunks.st: As a result, the lulav is then taken for seven days.

chunks.en: And on all the other days, six.
chunks.explain: Then one of the other days is Shabbos, and we do not take the lulav.
chunks.st: And if the first day occurs on one of the rest of the days of the week and one of the other days of the Festival coincides with Shabbat, the lulav is taken only six days.
chunks.stMore: Since the mitzva to take the lulav is a mitzva by rabbinic law throughout the rest of Sukkot, it does not override Shabbat.

summary: The aravah is done for seven days only when the seventh day of Sukkos is on Shabbos. Otherwise it is six days.

chunks.en: How is the aravah seven days?
chunks.st: The altar is encircled with the willow branch for seven days. How so?

chunks.en: If the seventh day of the aravah
chunks.st: If the seventh day of the mitzva of the willow branch

chunks.en: falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: occurs on Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: since on that day it is a mitzva by Torah law, it overrides Shabbat

chunks.en: the aravah is seven days.
chunks.st: and the mitzva of the willow branch is then performed for seven days.

chunks.en: And on all the other days, six.
chunks.st: And if the seventh day occurs on one of the rest of the days of the week, and one of the other days of the Festival coincides with Shabbat, since the mitzva of the willow branch is then by rabbinic law and consequently does not override Shabbat, it is performed for only six days.

summary: When the first day of Sukkos was on Shabbos, people left their lulavim on the Har HaBayis. Grabbing for them in the morning became dangerous, so the beis din made a rule that everyone takes the lulav at home.

chunks.en: How was the mitzvah of lulav done?
chunks.st: How is the mitzva of lulav fulfilled in the Temple when the first day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat?

chunks.en: If the first day of
chunks.st: If the first day of

chunks.en: the chag fell on Shabbos,
chunks.st: the Festival occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: they bring their lulavim to the Har HaBayis.
chunks.explain: They bring them before Shabbos.
chunks.st: all the people bring their lulavim to the Temple Mount

words.note: Har HaBayis is the mountain of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: The helpers take them from them and line them up
chunks.st: on Friday. The attendants receive the lulavim from them and arrange

chunks.en: on top of a bench.
chunks.st: them on a bench [itztaba],

chunks.en: And the Elders put theirs in a room.
chunks.explain: So they will not get pushed in the crowd the next morning.
chunks.st: while the Elders place their lulavim in the chamber.
chunks.stMore: They were given permission to do so due to the concern that they would be injured the following morning in the rush of people in search of their lulavim.

chunks.en: And they teach them to say,
chunks.st: And the court teaches the people to say:

chunks.en: "Whoever gets my lulav in his hand,
chunks.st: With regard to anyone whom my lulav reaches his possession,

chunks.en: it is his as a gift."
chunks.explain: Because on the first day one needs his own lulav.
chunks.st: it is his as a gift.
chunks.stMore: They did so to avoid the likely situation where people would inadvertently take lulavim that did not belong to them, as on the first day of the Festival one does not fulfill his obligation with a lulav that does not belong to him.

chunks.en: The next day, they come early,
chunks.st: The next day everyone rises early and comes to the Temple,

chunks.en: and the helpers throw the lulavim in front of them.
chunks.st: and the attendants throw the lulavim before them.

chunks.he: וְהֵן מְחַטְּפִין וּמַכִּין אִישׁ אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ.
chunks.en: And they grab them, and hit one another.
chunks.st: And in the confusion, the people snatch the lulavim and in the process strike one another.

chunks.he: וּכְשֶׁרָאוּ בֵית דִּין שֶׁבָּאוּ לִידֵי סַכָּנָה,
chunks.en: And when the beis din saw that it was getting dangerous,
chunks.st: And when the court saw that they came to potential danger,

words.note: Beis din is the court of the Sages.

chunks.en: they made a rule that each and every person
chunks.st: they instituted that each and every

chunks.en: should take his lulav in his house.
chunks.st: person will take his lulav in his house and fulfill the mitzva there.

summary: The aravah was done in the Beis HaMikdash: they brought big willow branches from Motza, stood them around the mizbe'ach, blew the shofar, and walked around the mizbe'ach while davening. On the seventh day they walked around seven times.

chunks.en: How was the mitzvah of aravah done?
chunks.st: How is the mitzva of the willow branch fulfilled?

chunks.en: There was a place below Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: There was a place below Jerusalem,

chunks.en: and it was called Motza.
chunks.st: and it was called Motza.

chunks.en: They go down there and gather from there
chunks.st: They would descend there and gather

chunks.en: big willow branches,
chunks.st: willow branches [murbiyyot] from there.

chunks.en: and they come and stand them up at the sides of the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: And they would then come and stand them upright at the sides of the altar,

words.note: The altar in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and their tops bend over the top of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: and the tops of the branches would be inclined over the top of the altar.

chunks.en: They blew a tekiah, a teruah, and a tekiah.
chunks.explain: These are sounds of the shofar or trumpets.
chunks.st: They then sounded a tekia, a simple uninterrupted blast, sounded a terua, a broken sound and/or a series of short staccato blasts, and sounded another tekia.

chunks.en: Every day they walk around
chunks.st: Each day they would circle

chunks.en: the mizbe'ach one time,
chunks.st: the altar one time

chunks.en: and say, "Ana Hashem hoshi'ah na,
chunks.st: and say: “Lord, please save us.

chunks.en: Ana Hashem hatzlichah na."
chunks.explain: "Please, Hashem, save us; please, Hashem, give us success."
chunks.st: Lord, please grant us success” (Psalms 118:25).

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says that they would say:

chunks.en: "Ani vaho, hoshi'ah na."
chunks.explain: Ani vaho is a special way of saying Hashem's name.
chunks.st: Ani vaho, please save us.

chunks.en: And on that day they walk around
chunks.explain: The seventh day of Sukkos.
chunks.st: And on that day, the seventh day of Sukkot, they would circle

chunks.en: the mizbe'ach seven times.
chunks.st: the altar seven times.

chunks.en: When they leave,
chunks.st: At the time of their departure at the end of the Festival,

chunks.en: what do they say?
chunks.st: what would they say?

chunks.en: "Beauty is yours, mizbe'ach!
chunks.st: It is beautiful for you, altar;

chunks.en: Beauty is yours, mizbe'ach!"
chunks.st: it is beautiful for you, altar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar said that they would say:

chunks.en: "To Hashem and to you,
chunks.st: To the Lord and to you,

chunks.en: mizbe'ach! To Hashem and to you, mizbe'ach!"
chunks.st: altar; to the Lord and to you, altar.

summary: The aravah was done on Shabbos too, but the branches were picked before Shabbos and kept fresh in golden pots. Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says they used palm branches.

chunks.en: As it is done on a weekday, so it is done on Shabbos,
chunks.st: As its performance during the week, so is its performance on Shabbat;

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיוּ מְלַקְּטִין אוֹתָן מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
chunks.en: except that they would pick them before Shabbos
chunks.st: except for the fact that they would gather the branches from Shabbat eve

chunks.en: and put them in golden pots,
chunks.st: and place them in basins of gold

chunks.en: so that they would not dry out.
chunks.st: so that they would not dry.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:
chunks.stMore: There was a unique custom on the seventh day.

chunks.en: they would bring palm branches,
chunks.st: They would bring palm branches to the Temple

chunks.en: and place them on the ground at the sides of the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: and place them on the ground at the sides of the altar,

chunks.he: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם נִקְרָא יוֹם חִבּוּט חֲרִיּוֹת:
chunks.en: and that day was called "the day of placing palm branches."
chunks.st: and that seventh day of Sukkot was called: The day of the placing of palm branches.

summary: On the seventh day of Sukkos, right after the mitzvah, the children took apart their lulavim and ate their esrogim, out of great joy.

chunks.en: Right away, the children take apart
chunks.st: Immediately after fulfilling the mitzva of taking the four species on the seventh day of the festival of Sukkot, children remove

chunks.en: their lulavim and eat their esrogim.
chunks.explain: They do this because they are so happy.
chunks.st: their lulavim from the binding and eat their etrogim as an expression of extreme joy.

summary: We say Hallel and have simcha on all eight days, including the last day, Shemini Atzeres. On the seventh day we may not take down the sukkah, but in the afternoon we bring our things into the house to honor the last Yom Tov.
stIntro: This mishna elaborates upon the first mishna in this chapter.

chunks.en: How are Hallel and simcha eight days?
chunks.st: The obligation to recite hallel and the mitzva of rejoicing on the Festival by sacrificing and eating the meat of peace-offerings are always for eight days. The mishna explains: How so?

chunks.he: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁחַיָּב אָדָם בַּהַלֵּל וּבַשִּׂמְחָה וּבִכְבוֹד
chunks.en: This teaches that a person must say Hallel, have simcha, and honor
chunks.st: This teaches that a person is obligated in hallel, and in the mitzva of rejoicing, and in reverence for

chunks.en: the last Yom Tov of the chag,
chunks.st: the last day of the Festival

chunks.en: just like all the other days of the chag.
chunks.st: like he is for all the other days of the Festival.

chunks.en: How is the sukkah seven days?
chunks.st: The mitzva of sukka is seven days. How does one fulfill this obligation for seven full days?

chunks.en: When he finished eating,
chunks.explain: On the seventh day.
chunks.st: When one finished eating

chunks.en: he should not take apart his sukkah,
chunks.explain: The mitzvah lasts until the end of the day.
chunks.st: on the seventh day, he should not dismantle his sukka
chunks.stMore: immediately, because the obligation continues until the end of the day.

chunks.en: but he takes the things down
chunks.st: However, he takes the vessels down

chunks.en: from Minchah time and on,
chunks.st: from the sukka into the house from minḥa time and onward

chunks.en: to honor the Yom Tov
chunks.st: in deference to

chunks.en: that is the last of the chag.
chunks.explain: The last Yom Tov is Shemini Atzeres.
chunks.st: the last day of the Festival, when he will require the vessels in the house.

summary: This mishnah tells how water was poured on the mizbe'ach on Sukkos. Water was brought with shofar blasts and poured into a silver bowl. Once a Tzeduki poured it on his feet instead, and the people threw their esrogim at him.

chunks.en: How was the water poured on the mizbe'ach?
chunks.st: With regard to the rite of water libation performed in the Temple during the Festival, how was it performed?

chunks.en: A golden jug that holds three
chunks.st: One would fill a golden jug with a capacity of three

chunks.en: lugin he would fill from the Shiloach spring.
chunks.explain: A log is a measure, about six eggs.
chunks.st: log with water from the Siloam pool.

words.note: A spring of water near Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: When they reached the Water Gate,
chunks.st: When those who went to bring the water reached the Gate of the Water,
chunks.stMore: so called because the water for the libation was brought through this gate leading to the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: they blew a tekiah, a teruah, and a tekiah.
chunks.st: they sounded a tekia, sounded a terua, and sounded another tekia as an expression of joy.

chunks.en: The Kohen went up the ramp and turned to his left.
chunks.st: The priest ascended the ramp of the altar and turned to his left.

words.note: The ramp that leads up to the mizbe'ach.

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי סְפָלִים שֶׁל כֶּסֶף הָיוּ שָׁם.
chunks.en: Two silver bowls were there.
chunks.st: There were two silver basins there
chunks.stMore: into which he poured the water.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: they were made of stone,
chunks.st: They were limestone basins,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיוּ מֻשְׁחָרִין פְּנֵיהֶם מִפְּנֵי הַיָּיִן.
chunks.en: but they looked dark because of the wine.
chunks.explain: So they looked like silver.
chunks.st: but they would blacken due to the wine
chunks.stMore: and therefore looked like silver.

chunks.en: And they had holes like two thin spouts,
chunks.st: The two basins were perforated at the bottom with two thin perforated nose-like protrusions.

chunks.en: one wide and one thin,
chunks.explain: The wide one was for the wine, and the thin one for the water.
chunks.st: One of the basins, used for the wine libation, had a perforation that was broad, and one, used for the water libation, had a perforation that was thin,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם כָּלִין בְּבַת אַחַת.
chunks.en: so that both would finish pouring at the same time.
chunks.st: so that the flow of both the water and the wine, which do not have the same viscosity, would conclude simultaneously.

chunks.en: The western one was for water,
chunks.st: The basin to the west of the altar was for water,

chunks.en: the eastern one was for wine.
chunks.st: and the basin to the east of the altar was for wine.

chunks.he: עֵרָה שֶׁל מַיִם לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל יַיִן,
chunks.en: If he poured the water one into the wine one,
chunks.st: However, if one poured the contents of the basin of water into the basin of wine,

chunks.en: or the wine one into the water one,
chunks.st: or the contents of the basin of wine into the basin of water,

chunks.en: he has done it. Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: he fulfilled his obligation, as failure to pour the libation from the prescribed location does not disqualify the libation after the fact. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: he would pour with one log all eight days.
chunks.st: The basin for the water libation was not that large; rather, one would pour the water with a vessel that had a capacity of one log on all eight days of the Festival
chunks.stMore: and not only seven.

chunks.en: And to the one pouring they say,
chunks.st: And the appointee says to the one pouring the water into the silver basin:

chunks.en: "Raise your hand!"
chunks.explain: So everyone can see that he pours the water into the bowl.
chunks.st: Raise your hand,
chunks.stMore: so that his actions would be visible,

chunks.en: Because one time someone poured
chunks.st: as one time a Sadducee priest intentionally poured the water

chunks.en: the water on his feet,
chunks.explain: He was a Tzeduki, who did not believe this was a mitzvah.
chunks.st: on his feet,
chunks.stMore: as the Sadducees did not accept the oral tradition requiring water libation,

chunks.en: and all the people threw their esrogim at him.
chunks.st: and in their rage all the people pelted him with their etrogim.

summary: On Shabbos the water could not be brought from the Shiloach, so it was filled before Shabbos and kept in a room. Water or wine left uncovered may not be used on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: As it is done on a weekday, so it is done on Shabbos,
chunks.st: As its performance during the week, so is its performance on Shabbat,

chunks.en: except that before Shabbos he would fill
chunks.st: except that on Shabbat one would not draw water. Instead, on Shabbat eve, one would fill

chunks.en: a golden barrel that was not made holy,
chunks.st: a golden barrel that was not consecrated
chunks.stMore: for exclusive use in the Temple

chunks.en: from the Shiloach,
chunks.st: from the Siloam pool,

chunks.en: and put it in a room.
chunks.st: and he would place it in the Temple chamber
chunks.stMore: and draw water from there on Shabbat.

chunks.en: If it spilled or was left uncovered,
chunks.explain: A snake may have put poison in uncovered water.
chunks.st: If the water in the barrel spilled, or if it was exposed
chunks.stMore: overnight, leading to concern that a snake may have deposited poison in the water,

chunks.en: he would fill it from the washing basin,
chunks.explain: The basin the Kohanim washed from in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: one would fill the jug with water from the basin in the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: because wine and water that were left uncovered
chunks.st: as exposed wine or water

chunks.en: may not be used on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: is unfit for the altar.
chunks.stMore: Just as it is prohibited for people to drink them due to the potential danger, so too, they may not be poured on the altar.
